summary: Elevated 503s after customer routing policy change (fallback disabled + region pin mismatch) — request safer config diff visibility during incidents
description:
Customer reports sudden spike in 503s after applying a routing policy change for their Dedicated deployment.

Issue summary
- NimbusCRM updated routing policy (via Console) to prefer eu-west for a subset of traffic and pinned a model variant for an internal “assistant-v2” route.
- Immediately after change, they observed elevated 503s on /v1/chat/completions and /v1/responses for that route.

Impact
- ~18–25% request failure rate (503) for route: assistant-v2 between 09:12–09:44 PT.
- Other routes remained stable.
- End users experienced degraded chat feature (intermittent failures, retries required).

Environment
- Dedicated cluster: nmb-ded-07
- Regions involved: us-east (primary), eu-west (new preference)

Customer-provided details
- Start time: 2025-02-18 09:12 PT
- Example request IDs (from customer logs):
  - req_01HQC2K3Z9X4R9P5YJ8V8Y8A1N
  - req_01HQC2M0B8P3JH2Y3A4M7ZQ2TT
- Symptom: 503 with body “upstream unavailable” (customer SDK surfaced as ServiceUnavailable)

What changed (per customer)
- Updated routing policy:
  - Increased weight to eu-west for assistant-v2
  - Disabled fallback routing (to avoid “unexpected model variants”)
  - Pinned model: redwood-llama-3.1-70b-instruct (customer label)

Support ask
1) Identify why this routing policy change results in 503s.
2) Provide guidance/guardrails to prevent recurrence.
3) Request: safer visibility into “what config changed” during incidents (customer noted that during incident response they couldn’t quickly confirm which flags/weights had actually propagated, and Redwood responders also had to manually hunt diffs).

resolution:
Root cause: customer routing policy pinned a model variant not provisioned/eligible in eu-west for their Dedicated pool while shifting 60% traffic to eu-west and disabling fallback routing. Router had no eligible targets in eu-west and returned 503.

Mitigation: customer set eu-west routing weight back to 0% (us-east 100%). Error rate returned to baseline within minutes.

Planned follow-up:
- Stage pinned model artifact to eu-west for nmb-ded-07 (scheduled maintenance window).
- Add guardrails/validation in routing policy editor: block or warn on region/model eligibility mismatches, especially when fallback is disabled.
- Improve incident-time visibility with a customer/tenant-safe config diff view (redacted) + propagation status and audit logging; align with incident-bot v2 work.
internal_notes:
Notes for SRE/Platform:
- This is a prime example for incident-bot v2 config-diff + routing context: on-call needed immediate visibility of routing weights, pinned model, fallback toggle, and whether the change propagated to all regions.
- Customer explicitly wants a safe diff they can reference during incident bridges (redacted; no secrets). Ensure any future implementation includes allowlist fields, secret detection, and audited access.
- Consider adding an automated preflight check for (tenant, route, model pin, region weights) -> eligible backends. If not, Console should block save or require explicit override.

- Slack: #incidents incident stub INC-2025-02-18-rcfg-503
- Similar pattern referenced in #incidents thread 1740345510-sev1-503s-after-config-push

Customer comms:
- Customer wants compliance-friendly behavior (fallback disabled by policy), so we should treat “fallback off” as a high-risk config and require stronger validation + warnings.
